text:
devin: Quick heads-up — I'm kicking off the rollout for the new runtime latency + KV-cache dashboards (runtime/latency, runtime/kv). Need to lock alerting rules + pager mapping before we flip traffic. cc @santosh @maya @emily :wave:

santosh: which exact metrics do you want on-call for vs just dashboarded?

devin: minimal set to start:
- p95_latency_ms (requests)
- p99_latency_ms
- cpu_util (per-gpu pool)
- kv_cache_hit_rate
- error_rate (http 5xx)

maya: I vote for two alarm classes:
1) SLO burn alerts (pager)
2) operational thresholds (paged only if sustained / resource saturation)

emily: routing rules idea:
- high cpu_util or OOMs -> eng-infra (infra team)
- high p95/p99 or kv_hit_rate drop -> runtime-oncall (runtime team)
- error budget burn (slo) -> product-oncall + runtime-oncall (both)

alex: agree on separation. Also want staging vs prod thresholds (staging = louder but no page).

santosh: can we share a starting prometheus alert snippet so PD services can be created?

devin: sure, sample (very rough):
```yaml
- alert: RuntimeHighP95Latency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    team: runtime
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/runtime-p95

- alert: KVCacheHitRateDrop
  expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[10m]) < 0.6
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: critical
    team: runtime
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/kv-cache
```

maya: for SLO burn we should use burn-rate > 2 over 1h for page, > 1 over 6h for warning. e.g.:
`burn_rate(slo_errors_total, 1h) > 2`

emily: paging mapping specifics:
- severity:critical -> page primary oncall (runtime-oncall) then escalate to eng-infra after 15m if label reason=cpu
- slo burn pages both product-oncall (for business impact) and runtime-oncall (for mitigation)

alex: do we have PD service names? I'd like `runtime-metrics-prod` and `runtime-metrics-staging` to match our infra naming.

ops-bot: Created PagerDuty service `runtime-metrics-prod` (service id svc_9a3). Linked escalation policy: Runtime Primary -> Runtime Secondary -> Eng-Infra.

devin: perfect. A couple of practical tuning notes:
- use `for:` windows to avoid noisy fleeting blips (10-15m for latency)
- use cohorting labels (region, pool, model_family) so we can mute specific noisy pools

santosh: runbook pointers? who writes them?

maya: I'll draft runbooks for the p95/p99/kv ones. assign to me. Will include quick mitigation steps: cache-warm, scale-pool, fallback-route.

emily: On the console side, I'll add the alert->dashboard links and a direct "ack & escalate" button to the runtime dashboard. Also will add a cost view so oncall knows impact of scale up ops.

alex: one more ask — add a burn-rate dashboard panel + small histogram for request sizes. Those helped us debug a previous incident.

devin: action items:
- maya: draft runbooks for runtime-p95, kv-cache (due EOD Thu)
- emily: add PD links & ack button on dashboard + cost panel (PR by Mon)
- santosh & alex: finalize alert thresholds and labels for staging vs prod (sync Tues 10am)
- devin: add the prometheus rules to the alert repo and coordinate canary rollout (canary window 48h)

ops-bot: Alerting PR created: https://git.redwood/alerts/pulls/412 — reviewers: devin, santosh, maya.

maya: got it, I'll start drafts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

emily: I'll carve out the console pieces tomorrow and post a preview link.

devin: thanks — let's keep noise low while we tune. If anyone sees weird flapping after canary, ping here.

alex: noted. I'll bring the staging thresholds and sample queries to Tuesday sync.

santosh: thanks.
